description: Demolition of existing buildings and the erection of a part four, part five-storey building, plus basement level to deliver a residential led mixed use building comprising 23 residential units (class C3), with commercial (class E) floorspace arranged over ground and lower ground floor levels.
decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The proposal, by reason of its excessive height and scale, within an established local spatial character that is predominantly low-rise, while also being located within a low-rise policy zone, would represent an unacceptable and incongruous transformative change within the location that would significantly harm the spatial character of the same location. The significant harm identified has not been outweighed by material considerations that indicate otherwise. As such, the proposal is considered to be contrary to the NPPF (2024) and Policies PM6 (Tooting Strategic Policy)) and LP4 (Tall and Mid-rise Buildings) of the Wandsworth Local Plan 2023.

Reason : 2 - The proposal by reason of its excessive scale, mass, layout and its elevational treatment represents poor quality design.  More particularly the proposal fails to address issues around the arrival experience, defensible space, refuse storage siting and surrounding poor public realm.  The proposals also fail to acknowledge context and character of the existing built form and can be said to be at odds with the need to achieve good design enshrined in the in the NPPF (2024) and more specifically Policy D3 of the London Plan (2021) (Optimising site capacity through the design-led approach) (Parts 11-14), Policy D8 (Public Realm) of the London Plan and Policy LP1(The Design-Led Approach) A; Parts 6, 8,10 & 11) of the Wandsworth Local Plan 2023

Reason : 3 - The proposal by virtue of its proposed height, mass, scale, appearance and its prominence on a rising curved stretch of Upper Tooting Road would result in a detrimental effect on the setting of and therefore, the significance of the Grade II listed, Kings Head Public House immediately to the north of the site and the Grade II listed Nos.68, 70 and 72 Upper Tooting Road also to the north of the site. It is also considered that the scheme would have a detrimental effect on the setting of, and therefore, the significance of a number of non-designated heritage assets, namely the Khalsa Centre Gurdwara opposite the site and the Former Pentecostal Church on Beechcroft Road. The public benefits of the proposals are not considered to outweigh the less than substantial harm caused to the significance of these designated heritage assets. Therefore, the development is contrary to Paras. 212-216 of the NPPF (2024), Policy HC1(Heritage Conservation and Growth) of the London Plan (2021) and Policy LP3 (Historic Environment (Strategic Policy)) of the Wandsworth Local Plan 2023.

Reason : 4 - The proposal is considered to be unacceptable in the interests of residential amenity. More particularly, the height and bulk of the proposed building and its close proximity to upper floor habitable room windows of the neighbouring residential property at No. 108 Upper Tooting Road that face Price Close, would result in an overbearing and dominating impact on the neighbouring residents. This would result in the harmful loss of daylight and outlook, and an increased sense of enclosure. Accordingly, the proposal would constitute an over dominant, inappropriate and un-neighbourly form of development and in this respect is contrary to the relevant provisions of Policy D6 (Housing quality and standards) of the London Plan (2021) Policy and LP2 (General Development Principles � Strategic Policy)) of the Wandsworth Local Plan 2023.

Reason : 5 - The proposal development provides an excessively high proportion of single aspect units of which three would face north with inset glazed facades and thereby fails to provide a suitably high quality of residential amenity for future occupiers contrary to Policy D6 (Housing Quality and Standards) of the London Plan (2021) and Policy LP27 of the Wandsworth Local Plan 2023.

Reason : 6 - The proposal fails to provide dedicated play and/or recreation space that would be required for a 23-unit residential scheme in this location and would thereby conflict with Policy S4 (Play and informal recreation) of the London Plan (2021) and Policy LP19 of the Wandsworth Local Plan 2023.

Reason : 7 - The proposal provides an insufficient quantum of units that meet Building Regulation M4(3) `wheelchair user dwelling� standards.  To meet Policy D7 of the London Plan (2021) two units at M4(3) standard are required. More generally London Plan Policy D5 requires the highest standards of accessible and inclusive design. The scheme provides no levels plans or Access Statement and wheelchair access and arrival experience through Price Close to the residential entrance is unacceptable. In the absence of detailed information and a failure to deliver sufficient M4(3) units the proposal does not achieve the highest standard of accessible and inclusive design and conflicts with both Policy D5 and D7 of the London Plan (2021) and Policy LP27 of the Wandsworth Local Plan 2023.

Reason : 8 - The proposal offers no short-stay cycle parking and locates resident cycle parking at basement  floor level.  Whilst overall resident provision is acceptable its difficult-to-reach location and incoherent route from the Price Close entrance through a lift and 3 single doors would discourage use and is likely to cause conflict with other residents.  Such an arrangement is in conflict with Policy T5 A&B (Cycling) of the London Plan (2021).

Reason : 9 - The proposal, by virtue of its layout and siting of refuse stores off Price Close and Holmbury Court would potentially compromise highway and pedestrian safety.  Refuse vehicles could not stop on Price Close nor on the adjacent Upper Tooting Road which is TLRN designated. The Applicant has failed to demonstrate how refuse in this location could be safely collected.  Furthermore, refuse vehicles using Holmbury Court would be required to utilise the narrow circular access road with its residents parking bays to avoid reversing, potentially giving rise to conditions prejudicial to highway and pedestrian safety.  As such this would conflict with Policy T4 (Assessing and mitigating transport impacts) of the London Plan (2021), Policy LP51.A.5 (Parking, Servicing and Car Free Development) of the Wandsworth Local Plan 2023 and the Council�s Reuse, Recycling and Waste Supplementary Planning Document Adopted (July 2025).

Reason : 10 - The proposal fails to comply and function in relation to the fire safety requirements with the accompanying Fire Statement lacking detail and clarity about such matters as evacuation lifts, detection and sprinkler systems and escape routes. The proposal is therefore in conflict with Policy D5(B5), Policy D12(A) and D12(B) of the London Plan (2021) and LP27 of the Wandsworth Local Plan 2023.

Reason : 12 - In dealing with this application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework and the Council has, as far as practicable, sought solutions to problems arising in relation to dealing with the planning application. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies in the Local Plan consisting of the Core Strategy, Development Management Policies Document, Supplementary Planning documents and where appropriate the Site Specific Allocations Document as well as offering a full pre application advice service. However, we have been unable to seek solutions to problems as the principle of the proposal is clearly contrary to our statutory policies and negotiation could not overcome the reasons for refusal.
